was: published as Ayer's 2010 annual town election, 11 contests, dated 2010-11-02
should_be: held: a party primary, not an annual municipal election
read: Section p1, first line: "Ayer Massachusetts Democratic Party Primary Election Results for Tuesday, September 14, 2010". Next: "Three-hundred seventy-seven (377) voters participated in this election. The following table records each candidate's vote total with a precinct by precinct breakdown." First office heading "Governor", then "Precinct 1 Precinct 2 Candidate". Eight of the record's 11 contests are Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State and Representative in Congress.
why: A party primary for state office is not the town's annual election and must not occupy its town-year slot. The parse is a faithful reading of the wrong election, so the fix is a different cut of the same report, not a re-read.

was: published as Palmer's 2004 annual town election, 17 contests, dated 2004-11-02
should_be: held: the state general election of 2 November 2004
read: The record's own office headings include "Representative in Congress", "Senator in General Court", "Representative in General Court" and "Sheriff". Its date is 2004-11-02, which is the Tuesday after the first Monday in November 2004. Section p1 carries the clerk's posting note: "MICHAEL P. STRZEMIENSKI, CLERK A truce copy, attest. I have this date posted attested copies in one public place in each of the four villages of the Town known as Depot Village, Thorndike, Three Rivers and Bondsville August 23, 2004".
why: No Massachusetts municipality elects a Representative in Congress or a Sheriff. This is the state general election printed in the town report beside the town's own return.

was: published as Salem's 2010 annual municipal election, 4 contests, dated 2018-11-06
should_be: held: the state general election of 6 November 2018
read: All four office headings in the record: "SENATOR IN CONGRESS", "GOVERNOR & LT. GOVERNOR", "ATTORNEY GENERAL", "SECRETARY OF STATE". Date on the record: 2018-11-06. The section carries no text layer, so the offices and the date are the whole of what can be read from the record itself; both say the same thing.
why: Four state offices and a 2018 date in a 2010 town-year slot. Salem's city election is in November of odd years and elects a Mayor and Councillors; none of those appears here.

was: published as Carver's 2014 annual town election, 9 contests, 13 named candidates, 22 vote totals
should_be: held: no figure and no name in the record appears anywhere in the document
read: The section is three pages. p1 is a scan of "TOWN OF CARVER STATEMENT OF CHANGES DETAIL AS OF JUNE 30, 2014" whose OCR is unreadable. p2, rendered at 150dpi and read as an image, is the report's INDEX, numbered 111: "Elections: / Annual Town Election Results, 4/26/14 .... 10 / State Election Results, 11/4/14 .... 19 / State Primary Election Results, 9/9/14 .... 13", then a department list, "Town Meetings: Annual Town Meeting Minutes, 6/16/14 .... 24". p3, rendered the same way, is blank. The record's first contest reads "Selectmen - Three for Three Years" with CHRISTOPHER WICKS 1185, RICHARD A. MURPHY 1098, WILLIAM D. O'NEIL 1012, JAMES P. MAILER 752. None of those names or figures is printed on p1, p2 or p3.
why: A contents page is a lead, not a return, and the reading taken from it is not supported by the document at any point. The election itself is on page 10 of the report, which this cut never reached. Held rather than corrected: nothing here can say what the true figures are.

read: The record dates itself 2016-04-04 and grounds 35 of 35 of its figures against its own section, so the reading is right; the filename is what disagrees. A town report is named for its fiscal year, which moves the date by one year at most, and 22 records here are one year off. Three years is not that.
why: A right reading in the wrong town-year slot. Refiling it under Freetown2016 is an operation on stems and artifacts, so it is the owner's, not this run's; meanwhile it must not stand as Freetown's 2019 election.
